# Five-rule integration fixtures

These new complete packages are generated by `build_five_rule_fixtures.py`,
using openpyxl only during construction, with targeted clean drawing alt metadata.
No checker results were used to generate an answer file. Historical fixtures and
JSON snapshots are unchanged. The tests never regenerate these saved inputs.

Both contain visible Data with A1:B2 formal Scores table (Name/Score, Ada/9), a
hidden worksheet with a chart sourced from Data!B2, merge A5:C5, and a hyperlink
at E5; Archive is veryHidden and empty. Relationships resolve to sheet1/sheet2,
table1 and drawing1; table ID and drawing object ID are 1.

- `five_rule_clean.xlsx`: the hidden tab is Objects; chart title/descr are
  Scores / Score for Ada; table header is enabled; merge is empty; E5 says
  Annual accessibility report. Expected: zero findings **within five rules**.
- `five_rule_seeded.xlsx`: hidden tab Sheet2, missing chart alt fields, disabled
  table header with matching existing plain labels and a body row, populated
  title merge A5:C5, E5 says click here. Expected: ALT_TEXT user input at drawing1
  #id=1, WORKSHEET_NAME user input at sheet2 #sheetId=2, TABLE_HEADER user input
  at table1 #tableId=1, MERGED_CELLS manual at sheet2 #merge=A5:C5, LINK_TEXT
  user input at sheet2 #cell=E5. The table is on a separate worksheet from the
  drawing/merge/link, so those features do not block header confirmation.

The hyperlink/title are disconnected one-cell components outside the table.
Both fixtures therefore disclose the single-cell/one-row/one-column inference
exclusion exactly once, without an extra table finding. A title merge is
intentionally screened by MERGED_CELLS. All expected tuples are authored in
`test_five_rule_integration.py`, with independent SHA-256 IDs.

Partial criterion references: 1.1.1 Non-text Content, 1.3.1 Info and Relationships,
2.4.2 Page Titled (related 2.4.6), 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context).
The test reads complete packages with openpyxl; no Microsoft Excel manual
no-repair inspection has occurred. No COLOR_CONTRAST or six-rule clean claim,
remediation, rendering or legal/WCAG compliance certification is made.

## Dedicated six-rule fixtures (corrected pack 2.1.1)

The five-rule inputs above retain their original bytes. The existing five-rule
integration test now exercises their five expected findings under the current
six-rule runner, also checking color assumptions and all six direct calls.

`six_rule_clean.xlsx` is a byte-identical new copy of the five-rule clean package,
now independently asserted clean within all six implemented screening rules.
`six_rule_seeded.xlsx` copies the five-rule seeded package and changes only:
styles.xml gets a new font (11pt, RGB 777777) and a new cellXf referencing it;
sheet1.xml cell B2 references that new style. Existing cells/styles are retained.
The exact six-rule oracle adds COLOR_CONTRAST / COLOR_OR_CONTRAST / Data /
xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml#cell=B2 / MANUAL_REVIEW to the five tuples above.
777777 on assumed white has ratio 4.478089453577214, below 4.5, per the independent
pack vector. It is grayscale, so this finding has only the low-contrast reason.
The expected limitation set is the table inference disclosure plus missing-fill
white assumption. No invented header or color meaning is involved.

`test_six_rule_integration.py` reuses the contract assertions (six actual calls,
five repeats, eight fields, independent IDs, immutable bytes, direct aggregation),
and adds sparse huge-dimension and malformed-XML failure checks. Shared use of
assertions does not copy production output into the oracle. Openpyxl reading is
verified; Microsoft Excel no-repair manual validation is still unperformed.
